the_structural_fact_that_shapes_this_who: Every URL in the manifest belongs to exactly ONE market, and distinct URLs per language equals rows per language exactly: en-GB holds 34,980 and en-US 49,299, together exactly the 84,279 distinct /en/ URLs. So the two English markets do not duplicate each other, they contribute DIFFERENT entities to a shared language space. That means a new market pays off in two different ways and they have to be ranked differently. A new LANGUAGE opens a new URL space and needs a new alternate-name pass, a new sitelink language and new local phrasing. A new MARKET IN AN EXISTING LANGUAGE needs none of that and still adds pages, but only for the entities the existing markets do not already search, which is exactly what separates en-AU from de-AT.

candidates.notes: REFUSED, and it is the cleanest demonstration of duplicate risk in the set. Austria shares /de/ with Germany and searches largely the same destinations, and the city things-to-do keywords come back at ZERO or ten: wien sehenswuerdigkeiten 10, salzburg 0, graz 0, innsbruck 10. Those queries exist, but the volume is attributed to the German market that already serves them. A second market in one language only pays when it searches DIFFERENT entities, which en-AU does and de-AT does not.

what_is_recommended_and_why: Materialise tr-TR first. It is the only candidate whose home country is captured in full, 195,140 POI and 23,717 places and 20,765 outdoor features and 14,553 parent polygons, and its city things-to-do family measures LARGER in Turkish than in most markets already built: eleven cities between 2,100 and 8,800 a month at difficulty 0. Nothing has to be downloaded for it. Then en-AU and es-MX, which need no new language at all and whose entities no existing market searches, as soon as the queue writes Australia and Mexico. Then ko-KR, which is unusual: its demand points at Japan, Spain, Italy and Taiwan, all captured, so it can be built before its own country is reachable. id-ID when the queue reaches Indonesia. th-TH and vi-VN are held, not refused: the demand is real and large and the half that carries it is network-blocked. ru-RU, ar-SA and de-AT are refused on the measurement, each for a different reason, and each reason is recorded.
what_this_does_not_do: It does not add a language for multiplication. Three candidates are refused and two are held, which is half the set, and the refusals are the point: ar-SA tops out at 300 a month, ru-RU has no advertiser bidding on the intent that monetises, and de-AT returns zero on the family that carries every other market because German already serves those queries.
